• Predictable Conditions: Calculate based on Total Body Weight (TBW) in obese patients. 
  
 • Ultra-short duration: Terminated by diffusion away from the junction. 
  
 • Defasciculating interactions: Dose must be increased if given after a defasciculating dose of a nondepolarizing NMBD.

• Calculation Basis: Nondepolarizing drugs should be calculated based on Ideal Body Weight (IBW) in obese patients to prevent relative overdosing and prolonged recovery. 
  
 • Inhalational Anesthetics: Continuous infusion doses are typically decreased by 30% to 50% when volatile anesthetics are used. 
  
 • Maintenance Timing: Supplemental doses should not be administered until quantitative monitoring shows the beginning signs of recovery.
• Rapid Tracheal Intubation: High doses can be used interchangeably with 1.5 mg/kg of succinylcholine to provide intubating conditions within 60 to 90 seconds.
• Without Intubation: If the trachea has already been intubated without an NMBD, a lower initial dose slightly less than the ED95 may be sufficient purely for surgical relaxation.
